solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Kind of band to speak fondly with agent about rock singer

parts.note: an Alice band is a hairband worn over the head
to coo is to murmur affectionately

indicators.note: 'about' here means turned round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative, an agent

explanation.surface: Someone talks affectionately with their agent about a rock star, and what sort of band he belongs to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of band' looks like a musical group, but it is the hairband named after the Alice in Wonderland illustrations.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice Cooper is an American shock-rock vocalist famous since the 1970s for theatrical stage shows.

clue.text: Reddish-brown uniform Yankee removed

indicators.note: something removed is taken away, so a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: livery is the uniform worn by servants or company staff
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A reddish-brown uniform is taken off a Yankee soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: LIVERY loses its Y to leave LIVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Liver as a colour adjective describes a dark reddish-brown shade, like the organ, used of dogs' coats.

clue.text: Nina and co excitedly touring unknown part of Manhattan?

indicators.note: touring means going all the way round, so one set of letters surrounds another
acting excitedly means moving about wildly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns

explanation.surface: Nina and her friends excitedly tour an unexplored district of New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manhattan' looks like the New York borough, but it is the cocktail; the question mark flags that. CINANO wraps round Z to give CINZANO.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinzano is a brand of Italian vermouth, and sweet vermouth is a key ingredient in the whisky cocktail.

clue.text: Fabric at the home of European swapped for interior

indicators.note: a swap trades one thing out and another in, so one letter is replaced

parts.note: chez is French for at the home of
E is the abbreviation for European
INT is a standard abbreviation for interior

explanation.surface: Fabric found at a European's house has been exchanged for something for the inside of the home.
explanation.walkthrough: In CHEZ the E is replaced by INT, giving CH-INT-Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Chintz is a glazed printed cotton cloth, usually with floral patterns, used for curtains and upholstery.

clue.text: As planned, arrive beyond Great Lake, dropping off final couple

indicators.note: dropping off the final couple means losing the last two letters
beyond means after, so one piece is placed following another

parts.note: Lake Ontario is one of North America's Great Lakes
to get somewhere is to arrive there

explanation.surface: A trip goes to plan: arriving past one of the Great Lakes and dropping off the last two passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping off final couple' reads as passengers getting out, but it cuts two letters from the lake's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on target means progressing exactly according to schedule or plan, an idiom taken from archery.

clue.text: Corresponding with US property agent endlessly bypassing question

indicators.note: to bypass is to go round something, so letters surround another piece
with no ends at all, both the first and last letters go

parts.note: realtor is the American term for an estate agent
QU is a standard abbreviation for question

explanation.surface: A message to an American estate agent who keeps dodging the question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' here removes both ends, not only the last letter, which is the usual reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Equal to means matching in value or amount, so one thing corresponds exactly with another.

clue.text: Like new game portraying comic character

parts.note: a la (French) means in the style of, like
N is the abbreviation for new
the partridge is a game bird

explanation.surface: A fresh game is being described as a portrayal of a funny character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like a pastime, but here it means birds shot for sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Partridge is the inept, self-important broadcaster created and played by British comedian Steve Coogan.

clue.text: Staple seen in front of old-fashioned dress

parts.note: a staple is a kind of pin or fastener
afore is an archaic word for before, in front of

explanation.surface: A basic item is spotted at the front of a dated frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old-fashioned' seems to describe the dress, but it marks the archaic word for in front of; 'Staple' is a fastener, not a basic commodity.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore is a sleeveless garment worn over a blouse, in Britain also called a pinafore dress.

clue.text: Beneath trees, following Masefield's first class poem

parts.note: a synonym

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of the poet's name
ilk means kind or class
a wood is a collection of trees

explanation.surface: A poem about lying under trees, after a fine one by John Masefield.
explanation.walkthrough: John Masefield was a Poet Laureate, which makes 'poem' feel like part of his phrase; Dylan Thomas wrote the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Under Milk Wood is Dylan Thomas's radio drama, a play for voices written in richly poetic verse-like prose.

clue.text: Make cheerful Alpine village housing westwards

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left
a house holds what lives in it, so the letters sit inside these words

parts.note: alpiNE VILlage holds the letters, read backwards

explanation.surface: A cheerful Alpine village with homes facing west.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters spanning alpiNE VILlage read right to left give LIVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To liven, usually liven up, is to brighten or enliven, making something more cheerful and animated.

clue.text: Interloping suitor's drunk inside pub

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: someone drunk is all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged; the 's is the verb is

explanation.surface: An uninvited admirer is drunk inside a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interloping' looks like an adjective for the suitor, but it is the definition, read as a noun: the act of interloping.
explanation.definitionFit: Interloping, used as a noun, is the act of intruding where one is not wanted, which is an intrusion.

clue.text: Wind one observes outside affected ears

indicators.note: outside means on both sides of, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: one who notes or observes is a noter

indicators.note: something affected has been altered, so the letters change order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wind blowing outside makes an observer's ears hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' seems to place the wind out of doors, but it tells one piece to wrap round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A nor'easter is a strong storm or gale blowing from the north-east, notably on the US Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Depart from open grassland before half five

indicators.note: before means coming first, so one piece precedes the next

parts.note: a lea is a meadow, open grassland

indicators.note: half means only two of the four letters are kept, here the back pair

parts.note: the second half of the written number

explanation.surface: Leaving the meadow just before half past five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half five' reads as the time 5.30, but it means half the letters of the word five.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a place is to depart from it, a straightforward synonym used as a transitive verb.

clue.text: Before meal, expert Latin figure roughly chopped

parts.note: a.p., ante prandium, is the Latin abbreviation for before a meal
a pro is an expert
X is ten in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A cook, before a meal, is an expert at rough chopping, like a Latin chef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly chopped' sounds like kitchen work, but it means the word for roughly, cut short: an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Approx is the standard short form of approximately, meaning roughly, so it is that word abbreviated.

clue.text: Soldier, fifty and flabby? It's an optical illusion

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
L is fifty in Roman numerals
lax means slack or flabby

explanation.surface: A fifty-year-old soldier who has gone soft is not what he seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flabby' sits in the surface as a description of the soldier, but it supplies its own piece, a synonym for slack.
explanation.definitionFit: Parallax is the apparent shift in an object's position when viewed from two different points, a visual effect.

clue.text: Jack stole, during further regressing, a large bottle

parts.note: J is jack in a pack of cards

indicators.note: during means in the course of, so one piece sits within another
regressing means going backwards, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: more means further, additional
a boa is a long scarf or stole

explanation.surface: Jack stole a big bottle while sliding further back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stole' looks like the past tense of steal, but it is the scarf. J then EROM wrapped round BOA.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeroboam is an oversized wine bottle, typically holding four standard bottles of champagne.

clue.text: Grass pitch with seventy-five pence lying on it?

parts.note: a quid is a pound, 100 pence, so three-quarters of the word is 75p
to sling is to throw or pitch

explanation.surface: A grassy sports pitch with some loose change dropped on it.
explanation.walkthrough: Quid is British slang for a pound; three-quarters of the word stands for 75p. In a down clue the coins lie on top of the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A grass is slang for an informer, and a quisling is a traitor who collaborates with an enemy.

clue.text: Clot in the European capital repeatedly missing last coach

indicators.note: missing last, done more than once, drops the final letter from each of two words

parts.note: taken as written
Rome is the capital of Italy
a coach is a kind of bus

explanation.surface: A fool in a European capital keeps missing the last coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clot' looks like an insult for a fool; it is the blood clot. THE and ROME each lose their last letter, then BUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrombus is the medical term for a blood clot formed inside a vessel or the heart.

clue.text: Period of growing charge by cabbies, picked up in London area

parts.note: May is a spring month when plants grow

indicators.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it, so the word is taken as spoken

parts.note: a fare is what a taxi driver charges

explanation.surface: Taxi drivers are raising their prices for passengers collected in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growing charge' looks like a rising price, but 'Period of growing' is a block on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayfair is an expensive district of central London's West End, also the priciest square on the British Monopoly board.

clue.text: Everyone conceals shop worker's error, primarily in addition

indicators.note: to conceal is to keep inside, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so the opening letters are used

parts.note: the opening letters of the three words

explanation.surface: All the staff cover up a shop assistant's mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL is split round S, W and E to give A-SWE-LL.
explanation.definitionFit: As well is an everyday phrase meaning too or also, adding something further to what was said.

clue.text: Put your foot down, training newsman to dissect sample?

indicators.note: to dissect is to cut into, so these letters go into the middle of another word

parts.note: to sup is to sip or taste, sample
PE is physical education, training
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A science teacher insists a trainee reporter dissect a specimen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put your foot down' looks like insisting firmly, but it is the driver pressing the accelerator; 'sample' is a verb, to taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting your foot down on the accelerator pedal makes the car go faster, so it means to accelerate.

clue.text: Stone rough-edged, mainly on right

indicators.note: mainly means most but not all, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: jagged means having rough, sharp edges
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A stone with rough edges, mostly on the right side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone' looks like a rock, but it is a member of the Rolling Stones. JAGGED loses its last letter and R follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Mick Jagger is the lead singer of the Rolling Stones, so he is a Stone.

clue.text: Scots here found missal many regularly dismissed

definitions.note: a place, read as somewhere Scots live

indicators.note: dismissing at regular intervals throws out every other letter

parts.note: the even-placed letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Scottish worshippers find many prayer books have been thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: A missal is a Catholic prayer book; dropping its odd letters together with those of 'many' keeps I, S, L, A, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Islay is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland, famous for its peaty whisky distilleries.

clue.text: It may trigger alarm in vehicle in a flash, leading to din

indicators.note: leading to means coming before, so one piece precedes the next
in means placed within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a sec, a second, is a flash of time
a car is a vehicle
a row is a noisy din

explanation.surface: A car alarm goes off in an instant and makes a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a car alarm; the alarm actually meant is that of birds in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarecrow is a figure set up in a field to frighten birds away, so it startles them.

clue.text: Ancient Scandinavian religion engulfs academic institution

indicators.note: to engulf is to swallow up, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: RC is Roman Catholic, a religion
uni is short for university

explanation.surface: An old Nordic faith takes over a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ancient Scandinavian religion' looks like one phrase, Norse paganism, but 'religion' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Runic describes the runes, the alphabet carved by early Norse and Germanic peoples.

clue.text: Greek ace seeing sweetheart changing imperceptibly

parts.note: GR is the abbreviation for Greek
A is ace in a pack of cards
dating is seeing a sweetheart regularly

explanation.surface: A champion Greek is quietly changing now he has a girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seeing sweetheart' is one idea: going out with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Gradating means passing by gradual stages from one shade or state into another, so the shift is barely noticeable.

clue.text: Pair guarding terminals in Newhaven search me

indicators.note: to guard is to surround protectively, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: a duo is a pair

indicators.note: terminals are the end points, so only the first and last letters count

parts.note: the first and last letters of the town

explanation.surface: A couple keep watch at the ends of Newhaven, but have no idea what is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: Newhaven is a ferry port on England's south coast. DUO wraps round the two Ns.
explanation.definitionFit: Search me is a colloquial way of saying I have no idea, and dunno is the slurred form of don't know.

clue.text: Film actor rejected some work involving bloodshed (a great amount)

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the letters are turned round

parts.note: the erg is a small unit of work in physics
gory means involving blood and violence
a peck, as in a peck of trouble, is a great deal

explanation.surface: A movie star turns down a violent role, apparently for a great deal of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some work' looks like a part or job, but it is a unit of work in physics.
explanation.definitionFit: Gregory Peck was a leading Hollywood star, an Oscar winner for To Kill a Mockingbird.
